pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 8.3.1 SENTENCE PATTERNS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentence Patterns

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentence Patterns
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How do we change a sentence from active to passive form?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. use active and passive voice correctly
2. use proverbs, phrasal verbs and idiomatic expressions in writing
3. create a narrative composition based on a given theme for self- expression

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentence Patterns

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentence Patterns

Teach
• Focus skill: use active and passive voice correctly.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentence Patterns.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentence Patterns
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we change a sentence from active to passive form?
2. Why is it important to plan your composition?
3. What makes a composition interesting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
